record.test_reason: A hackathon project, known only from its abstract in this roundup, reports its own result. Backup name mover heads (from the IOI circuit work) show similar backup behaviour when a head is interfered with in different ways, and backup-backup heads also exist. This bears on V5, backup heads as a named mechanism. The evidence is thin: no models, interventions or numbers are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say backup head behaviour is robust to the distribution used for ablation: different ways of interfering with a head elicit similar backup behaviour. They also say backup-backup heads exist and are similarly robust.
record.recipe_differences: The project varies how a head's function is interfered with and examines backup-head behavior, but the post does not specify the interventions or enough methodological detail to establish equivalence to the original studies' procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The summary says backup-head behavior is robust to the ablation distribution, but does not name or describe the distributions.
